bull_bear.body:
- **Policy: return ~85% of FCF cumulatively over the 5-year block FY25–FY29**, via semi-annual dividends and/or buybacks/special dividends; **progressively increasing DPS**.
- **~₹55,000cr returned over the last two years**; cumulative payout **82.1% of FCF** over two years; FY25-26 payout incl. buyback = **113.9% of FCF**.
- **₹18,000cr tender-offer buyback completed** — management defends it as **EPS-accretive and ROE-enhancing** (against heavy shareholder criticism that it destroyed value / was tax-unfavourable).
- **M&A = disciplined tuck-ins** to fill capability/segment white-spaces; strong cash gives speed on deals. Remaining ~15% of FCF funds these.
- **Bonus:** last bonus was 2019; multiple bonuses historically; **no bonus announced now** (repeatedly requested by shareholders).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Existential AI narrative / "AI inflation":** productivity deflation on legacy revenue; soft, cautious discretionary demand — the near-term growth swing.
- **CEO succession overhang:** shareholder flagged Salil Parekh's term up for renewal next year as "an overhang that needs to be cleared" — **notably NOT addressed** in management's answers. Watch-item.
- **Stock at 52-week low (~₹1,029–1,030)** vs ~₹2,000 last October; management "will not comment on share price."
- Guidance itself is a low bar (1.5–3.5% CC) — a shareholder even asked for guidance to be scrapped (peer TCS gives none); CFO defended it as reducing information asymmetry.
- Macro/geopolitics (Middle East, rates, FX) cited by shareholders; management leaned on 7-yr organic outperformance.
- FCF base-effect (tax refunds) makes YoY cash-flow optics look worse than reality.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, measured, "resilience" framing; heavy emphasis that **AI amplifies, not replaces** incumbents with enterprise context. Nandan: "skate to where the puck is going… the puck is coming to where we have already positioned ourselves."
- Transparent on the demand softness and "AI inflation"; candid that **execution risk (reorienting services, sales, talent, pricing to AI-first) is the real risk, not opportunity availability.**
- Deflected two hot investor topics — **CEO succession** and **share-price weakness** — without direct answers. Strong governance signalling (unqualified audit, ethics awards, ESG detail).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **AI revenue disclosure frozen:** the 5.5%/~$1bn AI-services figure is a Q3FY26 number merely "reconfirmed" — no refreshed AI revenue metric a full year on, despite explicit shareholder demand to report AI revenue separately. Suggests either lumpiness or reluctance to reset the anchor.
- **Guidance excludes Optimum acquisition** — so reported FY27 revenue will carry inorganic upside not in the 1.5–3.5% number.
- **Peer signalling on inorganic AI:** a shareholder cited **HCL investing in Sarvam AI** and asked if Infosys would buy a major AI company; CFO stuck to **tuck-in-only** discipline — a deliberate strategic divergence from a peer.
- **"Build vs buy" flips the software-vendor threat into a services tailwind** — enterprises retiring technical debt prefer to build, expanding the integrator's pie.
- FCF "decline" is entirely a FY25 tax-refund base effect — not deterioration.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **FY26 above-company-average growth:** Communications, Manufacturing, and Europe (all "significantly" above); Financial Services and the Services/Utilities/Energy/Resources grouping above average in CC.
- **FY27 acceleration expected:** Financial Services; Energy/Utility/Resources; Services grouping.
- M&A adds capability pockets: energy consulting (MRE), cybersecurity (Missing Link), Australia digital (Versent via Telstra JV), insurance/Guidewire (Stratus), US healthcare digital (Optimum Healthcare IT).
business.title: Segment / vertical detail

business.body:
- **Enterprise context / domain depth as the durable edge:** "Enterprise context is paramount… tools are accelerators." Management's repeated thesis is that the value is combining **agentic software with the traditional transaction systems** clients already run — something AI platforms cannot do without an integrator. That "convergence is where the next wave of opportunities will emerge."
- **Owned IP + partner ecosystem:** Topaz Fabric lets Infosys work with *any* foundation model; "all the big AI foundation-model companies and compute companies are working with Infosys" — foundation-model firms are "also approaching us."
- **Track record:** organic growth **fastest among peers for 7 consecutive years**; FCF >100% of PAT two years running; world's most ethical company 6 years (Ethisphere); fastest-growing IT-services brand 6 years (Brand Finance).

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 margin **held at 21%** despite macro negatives, cross-currency drag, pyramid changes, and acquisition dilution — plus absorbed higher S&M/AI investment. (FY25 had expanded +50bps.)
- Structural lever: **revenue per employee rising; revenue growing faster than headcount** via automation, pyramid and internal AI use (finance, marketing, coding).
- **"AI inflation" / productivity deflation** is the acknowledged revenue headwind — client productivity savings are (partly) recycled into new IT spend, expanding the addressable market rather than pure leakage.
- On AI margin question: management would not label AI margin-accretive/neutral/dilutive but pointed to the medium-term intent to lift margins.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 / 45th AGM (this):** FY26 closed — $20.2bn rev (+3.1% CC), 21% adj. margin, $3.7bn FCF (112.6% PAT), $14.9bn TCV (55% net-new), 41 clients >$100m, attrition 12.6%, ~328k heads. FY27 guide reaffirmed **1.5–3.5% CC / 20–22% margin** (ex-Optimum). AI services ~5.5%/~$1bn (Q3 figure reconfirmed). ₹18,000cr buyback done; dividend ₹48 (+11.6%); ~₹55,000cr returned in 2 yrs (82.1% of FCF). Board: Nitin Paranjpe → Vice Chairman (Apr 30 '26); Diane Jurgens (ID, Apr '26); Helene Potier reappointed. Stock at 52-wk low ~₹1,030. CEO succession + share price not addressed.
- _Q1FY27 quarterly results → check: does FY27 CC growth track toward 1.5–3.5%? refreshed AI-revenue % (still frozen at 5.5%?); FS / Energy-Utilities-Resources acceleration; margin within 20–22%; CEO succession clarity; Optimum inorganic contribution._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27: 1.5% to 3.5% constant currency** — reaffirmed from the April 2026 results; **excludes the Optimum acquisition** completed this quarter.
- **Operating margin FY27: 20% to 22%.** Medium-term "endeavour is to improve margins from current levels."
- **No guidance given for years beyond FY27** (CFO explicit).
- **AI-first services TAM: US$300–400bn addressable by 2030** across the six value pools (Nandan cited "close to $300bn IT spend by 2030"; CFO/Salil cited $300–400bn).
- **AI services run-rate: ~5.5% of revenue (~US$1bn annualized), growing faster than company average** (metric last formally disclosed at Q3FY26; reconfirmed, not updated).
- FY27 vertical outlook: **acceleration expected in Financial Services, Energy/Utilities/Resources, and the Services grouping.**
- Hiring: plan to **increase** the number of college graduates brought in vs FY26's 20,000.
- No new/changed capital-allocation or dividend policy — existing 85%-of-FCF policy runs through FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- FY26 large-deal TCV **US$14.9bn, 55% net-new**, deal wins **+24% YoY**. Beyond large deals, a broad book of medium/small deals.
- Pipeline skewed to **AI services + modernization**; clients moving from AI pilots to **enterprise-wide** deployment. Rising **AI-first GCC** activity flagged as a conversion channel.
- Demand environment described as **soft / cautious** on macro concerns; growth also dented by "AI inflation."
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Six AI value pools** ($300–400bn TAM to 2030): AI engineering & strategy; Data; Process/agents; **Modernization (called out as the largest near-term area)**; Physical AI (manufacturing/medical/automotive); AI Trust.
- **Scale metrics:** 90% of top-200 clients engaged on AI; 90% of employees "AI aware"; **4,800+ AI projects; 600+ agents built**; forward-deployed-engineer team scaling; 16 analyst AI leadership rankings.
- **"Build vs buy" tailwind:** AI has made legacy modernization urgent; clients retiring decades of technical debt and preferring to build — "creates even larger opportunities for us."
- Innovation engine: Center for Emerging Technology & Solutions (incubating AI, ML, quantum), Infosys Living Labs (with universities in UK & US), Springboard digital skilling (15M reached in India; 10M+ worldwide free).
- Optionality: quantum computing incubation; outcome-based / new pricing models being explored.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 was a "resilience" year — US$20.2bn revenue (+3.1% CC), 21% adjusted margin, US$3.7bn FCF (112.6% of PAT), US$14.9bn large-deal TCV (55% net-new) — but the stock sits at a 52-week low (~₹1,030, down from ~₹2,000 last October) as the market prices an existential AI question ("if coding is automated, why are we needed?"). Management's whole answer is the AI-services pivot: an AI-first TAM of **US$300–400bn by 2030**, AI services already ~5.5% of revenue (~US$1bn annualized, growing faster than company average), Topaz Fabric + a partner ecosystem, and a FY27 guide of **1.5–3.5% CC growth at 20–22% margin**. The near-term swing factors are soft discretionary demand + "AI inflation" (productivity deflation on legacy revenue); the long-term bet is that AI *amplifies* incumbents with deep enterprise context rather than replacing them.

open.item: Including the FY26 buyback and dividends, the Company has returned approximately ₹55,523 crore (82.1% of cumulative free cash flow for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026) toward its Capital Allocation Policy target of returning approximately 85% of free cash flow cumulatively over a five-year period.
open.promised: 82.1 % of cumulative FCF (2 of 5 years elapsed)

open.item: The Board recommended a final dividend of ₹25 per share (on top of an interim dividend of ₹23 per share already paid), for a total FY26 dividend of ₹48 per share; the final dividend is subject to shareholder approval at the AGM on June 23, 2026, with record date June 10, 2026 and payment on June 25, 2026.

Effective from fiscal 2025, the Company expects to continue returning approximately 85% of free cash flow cumulatively over a five-year period through semi-annual dividends and/or share buybacks/special dividends, and to progressively increase annual dividend per share (excluding special dividend).

The Company continued running Project Maximus, a margin-expansion program structured across five pillars (value-based selling, efficient pyramid, lean/automation/gen-AI, improving key portfolios, and optimization of indirect costs) to fund investment in talent, AI, and sales and marketing.
Continuous focus on re-skilling the company's over 3,25,000 employees on AI to support the pivot to AI-first services.
Launched a focused growth program targeting large global companies where Infosys currently has a smaller share of client spend, described as rapidly developing into a key growth driver.

The US Department of Justice is investigating how the Company classified certain H-1B visa-recipient employees working for one client in immigration filings; outcome and materiality cannot be predicted.
Infosys remains committed to recharging more water than it consumes by 2030, as part of its climate-positive aspirations and water stewardship strategy.

Infosys continues to progress towards its goal of zero waste to landfill, guided by circular economy principles; it has already achieved 99% waste diversion from landfill and certified 11 campuses as True Zero Waste in fiscal 2026.
Management sizes the incremental AI-first services opportunity opened by its AI-first value framework and Infosys Topaz at USD 300-400 billion by 2030, per market estimates.
